subject: Re: Skyline AI — capacity commitment term and GPU price sensitivity
messages:
From: Alexis Martin <alexis@skylineai.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@skylineai.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Reserved capacity proposal — term question + GPU price sensitivity

Sean —

Thanks for the term sheet earlier this morning. A couple questions from our procurement team as we prep internal approvals:

1) We currently plan to commit to a 24-month reserved capacity block, but given recent GPU price swings our CFO is pushing for a built-in price protection clause or a mid-term repricing trigger tied to an agreed market index.

2) If Redwood were to offer a ramped discount (tiered by utilization milestones) in lieu of a hard price index, what’s the maximum discount band you can sign off on without escalating to finance?

We also attached a short model showing sensitivity to GPU cost movements — curious if Redwood can build a 12-month review window with either an indexation or an agreed top-up/credit mechanism.

We’d like to finalize commercial terms by Mar 12 if possible. Can you advise next steps / approval path on your side?

—Alexis
Alexis Martin
Head of Infrastructure Procurement | SkylineAI
Attachment: cost-sensitivity-model.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alexis Martin <alexis@skylineai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity proposal — term question + GPU price sensitivity

Alexis —

Appreciate the model — I reviewed it and looped in Karthik (sales ops) and Kimberly (commercial finance). High level:

- We can include a 12-month commercial review window. There are two practical levers we can offer: (A) an indexation-style adjustment tied to a published GPU spot index (subject to a +/- floor/ceiling), or (B) utilization-driven rebates/credits (tiered discounts applied retroactively at review).
- The index approach is cleaner operationally but requires legal sign-off on cap/floor guardrails. The rebate approach is easier to pay out but reduces post-hoc visibility for your forecasting.

Before I escalate to my VP for any exceptions, can you confirm which structure you’d prefer and a target maximum downside protection (e.g., a 10% cap on pass-through to you)? That will help us size an approval ask.

I’ll put together a short approval memo once you confirm.

Best,
Sean
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Alexis Martin <alexis@skylineai.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@skylineai.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 08:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity proposal — term question + GPU price sensitivity

Sean —

Thanks — we prefer option B (utilization-driven rebates) because our procurement team wants predictability on list price and to realize credits if utilization under-delivers vs plan.

Target ask: a 12-month review with up to a 12% retroactive rebate if realized utilization is below the agreed baseline by more than 15%. If possible, we’d like a pathway to convert a portion of the rebate to a one-time credit applicable to future months in the 24-month term.

Can your memo recommend a maximum rebate band you can approve without Marissa/exec sign-off?

Alexis
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Skyline AI — capacity commitment term and GPU price sensitivity (approval memo)

Marissa —

Forwarding the ask from Skyline. Key points for your review:

- Customer: SkylineAI (prospect moving to committed reserved fleet)
- Ask: 24-month reserved commit; they want a 12-month utilization review with up to 12% retroactive rebate if utilization < baseline by >15%. They also want option to convert rebate to future-month credit.
- Proposed Redwood playbook: allow up to 6% rebate as a finance-delegated concession. Anything >6% requires VP approval + legal to add a convertible-credit clause.
- Risks: higher rebate increases unit economics exposure if GPU prices spike upward (we hedge but not fully). The attached sensitivity model shows downside at 10-15% rebate levels.

Attachment: Skyline_TERM_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: cost-sensitivity-model.xlsx (xlsx)

Request: Marissa — can you authorize up to 9% rebate as an exception for strategic customers, or should we hold firm at 6%? If you approve 9%, we will require a small one-time non-refundable onboarding fee and an exec-level credit cap.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Skyline AI — capacity commitment term and GPU price sensitivity (approval memo)

Karthik / Sean —

Thanks for the memo and the sensitivity attachments. I’ve reviewed Skyline’s ask and the modeled exposures. Given SkylineAI’s platform profile and likely ARR, I approve the following concession path as an exception:

- Approve up to a 9% retroactive rebate at the 12-month utilization review, subject to:
  - A mandatory one-time onboarding fee of $75k (non-refundable) to offset provisioning risk.
  - A cap that any convert-to-credit amount cannot exceed 50% of the rebate value and must be used within the next 6 months of the credit issuance.
  - Legal to insert a simple cap/floor on any pass-through linked to a publicly available GPU index (for transparency).
  - Finance to sign off on the final SOW numbers and expected unit economics before countersignature.

Karthik — route this to Legal and Finance. If they raise material objections, loop me back immediately. Sean — share an updated SOW with Skyline and include the DocuSign link once legal signs off.

Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial | Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alexis Martin <alexis@skylineai.com>
Cc: contracts@skylineai.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 16:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Skyline AI — capacity commitment term and GPU price sensitivity

Alexis —

Good news: leadership has approved a one-time exception path. Summary of agreed commercial guardrails: 24-month reserved commit with a 12-month utilization review. If realized utilization is below baseline by >15% we will provide a retroactive rebate up to 9% (subject to the following):

- One-time onboarding fee: $75,000 (non-refundable)
- Up to 50% of the rebate may be converted to a credit against future invoices; converted credits must be used within 6 months of issuance
- Final SOW will include a simple cap/floor for pass-through tied to a public GPU index for transparency
- Legal and Finance sign-off required; we will send an updated SOW and DocuSign link by end of day tomorrow contingent on their review.

Next steps: I’ll circulate the revised SOW (attached) and the DocuSign packet. Please review and confirm you’re comfortable with the onboarding fee and the credit conversion limit, and we’ll proceed to countersign.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the finish line.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
Attachment: Skyline_TERM_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)
Link: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/skyline-sow-0311
